cell_2: Measure and scope
Preliminary BSAI fishery management plan (FMP), including closure areas.
BSAI groundfish FMP implemented; Chinook salmon bycatch limits established for foreign trawlers.
BSAI groundfish optimum yield capped at 2 million t; Chinook salmon bycatch limits for foreign trawling reduced.
Domestic observer program and associated data reporting began.
Pollock allocations under the Western Alaska Community Development Quota (CDQ) program began.
Prohibited Species Donation Program established in 1993; voluntary salmon donations in 1994 are reported in the accepted assessment history.
Council recommended minimum codend mesh/design standards; an implemented NMFS mesh rule is not established by the reviewed sources.
NMFS began publishing individual-vessel bycatch rates online.
Emergency Chum Salmon Savings Area in 1994; permanent chum savings-area provisions under Amendment 35 in 1995, alongside the historical Chinook closure/trigger regime.
Amendment 49 improved retention/utilization requirements for pollock and Pacific cod took effect January 3.
American Fisheries Act (AFA) enacted, establishing the framework for sector allocations and fishery cooperatives.
AFA provisions implemented for catcher/processors.
Emergency rule introduced temporal and spatial pollock dispersal measures and trawl exclusion zones around selected Steller sea lion rookeries and haulouts in the BSAI and GOA.
AFA provisions implemented for the remaining catcher-vessel and mothership sectors.
Pollock industry began the voluntary chum salmon rolling-hotspot program.
Pollock industry began the voluntary Chinook salmon rolling-hotspot program.
Council selected Amendment 84 in October to provide a salmon bycatch intercooperative agreement (ICA) alternative to fixed savings-area closures.
The B-season exempted fishing permit tested the ICA/rolling-hotspot approach before general regulatory implementation.
Amendment 84 regulations, effective November 28, exempted pollock vessels participating in an approved salmon bycatch ICA from specified savings-area closures.
Amendment 91 final rule effective September 29, 2010; Chinook PSC limits, incentive plan agreements (IPAs), performance standards and enhanced monitoring operated in the 2011 fishery.
Council took final action on Amendment 110 in April, recommending linked Chinook/chum avoidance measures and abundance-based Chinook limits.
Amendment 110 final rule published June 10, effective July 11. It strengthened IPAs and changed pollock seasonal allocations to 45% A season / 55% B season.
First fishing year informed by the Amendment 110 three-system abundance index in 2016. Low-abundance limits apply when the index is at or below 250,000 Chinook salmon.
